<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of the [ORG_1_NEW] Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase customer choice. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling logistics network instead of school lunches.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study. Chief Minister Kumar needs to make the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications. For instance, what happens to PDS contracts? Will they be assigned to AgriIndia? Will customers in [LOC_1_NEW] have the right to choose going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that customers can make their own agricultural commodity decisions going forward. We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is giving customers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full. If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehousing purchase in this deal? May never happen. Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through securitization and through the [EIX_NEW] refund to AgriIndia and get on with it.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Western India [ORG_6_NEW] of Understanding:

? Commitment to Provide Grains =01) AgriIndia will keep its current grain processing plants and other agricultural assets and commit them to provide produce on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years. ? [ORG_7_NEW] =01) [ORG_8_NEW] will commit the entire output of [LOC_2_NEW] (one of [ORG_9_NEW] non-regulated farming facilities) to the [ORG_10_NEW] on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of [LOC_2_NEW] is to be brought online by August 14, 2024. If not brought online by August 14, 2024, [ORG_8_NEW] shall be assessed a ₹1.6 crore penalty. ? Aahana Varughese =01) AgriIndia will sell to the [ORG_10_NEW] its warehousing assets for approximately ₹230 crore (2.3 times the net book value of the assets), subject to certain adjustments.
